chapter: Hampton, Andy Kirk and Charlie Barnet
title: Joining Charlie Barnet: raises and gambling
summary: He moves to Barnet, who pleads poverty but throws away money gambling, and later holds him to a contract after a layoff.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, I went with Charlie Barnet, see. And that made a difference, because Charlie...

In '42, I think. Yeah, I think it was at that time. But then, I really traveled after that...with Barnet, I mean. I went back with Kirk, because Charlie said he was going to take off six months -- he didn't want to play no more for a while. And after he was off a month, he called me up... I was with Andy, and he called me up telling me he got a contract on me; and I didn't remember signing no contract with him.
Well, how long had you been with Barnet when he decided to lay off for a while?
I remember you telling me that you'd asked him for a raise, and he would cry poverty, and yet he'd be out gambling...
And losing all his money. Yeah, I was telling you about when he was in Atlantic City. He was

Yeah. He was shooting dice. It wasn't like it is now! But man, this cat, he would throw away more money in one night than I had made in a whole damn year. Then I asked him for a raise and he wouldn't give me a raise. I said, "Oh boy, this cat is something. It's hard to believe a motherfucker could be like this." And he'd take me out with him and let me see him doing it. Then when I asked him for some money, he said "No!" Man...
